title: I Posted the Office Snack-Fund Ledger After the Chips Vanished

parts.text: I opened the snack drawer at 3:06 p.m. and the kettle chips I had restocked on Monday were gone, ledger unpaid. The honor system QR was my idea; the unpaid line was not. I was twenty-nine, office manager, holding a receipt. I posted the ledger in the kitchen Slack, names of paid, blank for chips. Then I restocked pretzels, which are less beloved. At 3:14 a designer named Cole said Slack was aggressive, from a desk that still had kettle crumbs.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Cole is calling Slack aggressive with crumbs on the desk.

social.video_title: Honor-system chips, blank ledger, crumbs — Part 1/2
social.description: Monday restock, QR, kitchen Slack. Pretzels went in. Would you have named Cole?

parts.text: Cole Venmo'd. The ledger got a check. I brought chips back. Slack stayed a kitchen. Aggressive is a word for arithmetic on a wall. Honor systems need a public board or they are a donation jar for the bold. I keep receipts. Crumbs are a confession. Pretzels remain as a backup personality. The drawer closes louder when it is honest.

social.description: Chips returned, check in ledger, pretzels as backup. Was Slack a shaming or a till?
